issues.legal_issue: A constitutional writ court does not exceed its jurisdiction by directing redevelopment and supervising implementation where the parties consented to the project and the directions address public obstruction while protecting affected occupants.
material_facts: The proceedings included a public-interest petition concerning obstruction of public ways and separate writ petitions by the market shopkeepers.
The market was congested, vehicles had difficulty passing, and goods placed on the street prevented members of the public from using the footpath.
The shopkeepers consented on several occasions to construction of a new market, and a committee was constituted with their consent to address implementation issues.
The directions provided for temporary alternative accommodation and for allotment of ground-floor shops to existing shopkeepers after construction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court did not overstep its jurisdiction in issuing the redevelopment and supervisory directions; those directions could not be faulted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the challenged directions made in proceedings under Article 226 in light of the parties’ repeated consent, the public obstruction shown by the record, and the protections for the existing shopkeepers. It did not rely on earlier cases, stating that there was no need to address the cited decisions.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_writ_court_directions and shopkeepers_consented_to_redevelopment and public_access_was_obstructed and directions_protected_existing_occupants

predicates.appeal_challenges_writ_court_directions: The proceeding is an appeal challenging directions issued by a writ court.
predicates.shopkeepers_consented_to_redevelopment: The affected shopkeepers repeatedly agreed to redevelopment during the proceedings.
predicates.public_access_was_obstructed: The existing market conditions obstructed public passage or use of public ways.
predicates.directions_protected_existing_occupants: The directions provided safeguards for existing occupants during redevelopment and afterward.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges writ-court directions, the shopkeepers consented to redevelopment, public access was obstructed, and the directions protected existing occupants, the directions are not beyond the writ court’s jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A redevelopment project approved by a competent planning authority may proceed only in accordance with the required authority and applicable statutory requirements.
material_facts: A planning permission for reconstruction had been granted by a Joint Director of the planning department.
It was argued that the Director had objected and that further State approval was required.

The Court regarded the Joint Director as the competent officer but stated that construction must not proceed without the authority of the person concerned or contrary to statutory provisions and regulations.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the planning permission was rejected, subject to construction being carried out only with competent authority and in compliance with applicable statutory requirements.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the competent officer’s permission as sufficient to reject the objection presented, while requiring compliance with the applicable statutory provisions and regulations.

predicates.appeal_challenges_redevelopment_permissi: The proceeding challenges permission for a redevelopment project.
predicates.competent_planning_officer_granted_permi: An officer regarded as competent granted planning permission for the project.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges redevelopment permission and a competent planning officer granted it, the redevelopment must proceed with competent authorization and in accordance with applicable requirements.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge concerning amounts deposited by occupants does not warrant relief where the amounts are to be adjusted against future licence fees and consent to redevelopment continued.
material_facts: The shopkeepers deposited an amount after agreeing to contribute toward the proposed market arrangements.
The Municipal Corporation stated that the amount was not for construction charges but would be adjusted against future licence fees.
Consent to the redevelopment process continued after applications concerning earlier orders and the deposited amounts were made.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no substance in the deposit-related challenge.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the stated purpose of the deposits and the continued consent to redevelopment in rejecting the challenge; it identified no separate statutory provision or earlier case as governing this issue.

predicates.appeal_includes_deposit_related_challeng: The proceeding includes a challenge concerning amounts deposited during the underlying proceedings.
predicates.deposited_amount_was_for_future_licence_: The deposited amount was stated to be adjustable against future licence fees rather than construction charges.
predicates.consent_to_redevelopment_continued: The affected occupants continued to consent to redevelopment after raising the deposit-related challenge.

issues.definition: When an appeal includes a deposit-related challenge, the deposit was for future licence fees, and consent to redevelopment continued, the challenge does not warrant relief.

issues.legal_issue: Existing occupants who remain eligible must receive ground-floor shops in the rebuilt market after the ground floor and required parking facilities are completed.
material_facts: The redevelopment plan provided for ground-floor shops for the existing market shopkeepers.

The Court directed that, after construction up to ground-floor level and completion of the required basement parking facilities, shops be allotted to the old shopkeepers within six months, unless an individual shopkeeper became ineligible.
issues.conclusion: The old shopkeepers were to be allotted shops after the specified construction was completed, subject to individual ineligibility.
issues.legal_principle: The Court gave effect to the directions protecting existing shopkeepers and expressly conditioned their allotment on eligibility and completion of the ground floor and required parking facilities.

predicates.redevelopment_appeal_is_before_the_court: The proceeding concerns an appeal about directions for market redevelopment.
predicates.existing_occupant_remains_eligible: An existing occupant remains eligible to receive a shop in the rebuilt market.
predicates.ground_floor_and_required_parking_are_co: Construction has reached the ground floor and the required parking facilities are complete.

issues.definition: When a redevelopment appeal is before the Court, an existing occupant remains eligible, and the ground floor and required parking are complete, eligible existing occupants are allotted ground-floor shops.
